messages.author: 71879c31fafddeee
messages.subject: parcelAllocation query
parts:
lavaan Users, 

I have been running some models using the parcelAllocation function in semTools with lavaan. This implements Sterba and MacCallum's (2010) procedures for assessing item-parcel allocation variability. I have noticed that the fit summary provided by parcelAllocation output gives some strange results. 

For example, in all my runs (multiple models with different estimators) CFI average fit comes back as 0.000 as does its standard deviation etc. RMSEA for the same model fit with ML and MLM comes up with wildly different and implausible looking numbers (-151968.0 and 0.926 respectively).

Across all models, the estimator used makes quite a difference to how the values appear, and whether they seem to be in a sensible range for that index. The only fit index which consistently seems to give a) plausible values in the correct range for that index, and b) values I would expect for the models I am fitting, is the TLI. 

It is quite possible I have made an error, or that I am misunderstanding these values, but it seems like the function may be pulling the wrong numbers from the lavaan objects. This would make sense, for example, if the lavaan objects are different shapes for the different estimators.

Has anyone else had this problem, or does anyone have any suggestions where I may be going wrong?

Thanks

Tom

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: parcelAllocation query
parts:
Looks like a bug in the parcellAllocation function. We'll get it fixed and a new version of the function added to the next update in semTools.

Thanks!

-Alex
